clue.text: Mock journalist about journey by bike

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned round, so the preceding word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
you ride a bicycle, and a trip on one is a ride

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a reporter who cycles to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride someone is to ridicule or scorn them, a direct synonym of the verb mock.

clue.text: Slaver over tailless river bird

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' suggests turning upside down, so the whole build is read in the opposite direction
without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the Elbe is a major German river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog drools over a bird that has lost its tail by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' looks as if it applies to the bird, but it cuts the river; 'Slaver' is the verb to drool, not a slave trader.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, which is what dribble means.

clue.text: Woman involved in resistance on French island produces a gun

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: île is French for island
F is short for female

explanation.surface: A female Resistance fighter on a French island brings out a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, so it is a type of gun.

clue.text: Extremely enthusiastically supports alcoholic in his normal manner of behaving

definitions.text: in his normal manner of behaving

parts.note: a drunk is an alcoholic

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only letters from its start and finish are kept

parts.note: two letters from each end of the word

explanation.surface: A cheerleader backs a drinker who is behaving the way he always does.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supports' means sits underneath, so the ends of enthusiastically go below DRUNK. The definition is how an alcoholic normally behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: For an alcoholic, the habitual way of acting is while intoxicated, so the adverb describes his usual behaviour.

clue.text: Former buxom model

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, and the prefix ex- means former
buxom means full-figured, ample

explanation.surface: A description of a curvy woman who used to work as a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a catwalk model, but it means a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A model in the sense of an ideal to be copied is an example, as in 'set an example'.

clue.text: Teen gal could be stylish

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenage girl may turn out to be fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Adult sex drive won't do as a defence

indicators.note: here the phrase is read as refusing a word, so that short word is taken out

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
libido is sexual desire

explanation.surface: A grown-up's sexual appetite is no excuse in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't do' looks like a verdict on the excuse, but it tells you to remove the letters D and O spelling 'do'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere when a crime happened, used as a defence in court.

clue.text: Undergarment I cover with favourite tee on top

parts.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter
taken as written
a coat is a covering, such as a coat of paint

explanation.surface: Someone says they hide their underwear by wearing their best T-shirt over it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top' places the favourite and the letter above the rest; 'tee' is the letter's name, not a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a light skirt worn beneath a dress, so it is a garment worn underneath.

clue.text: European progressive edges away from exit

indicators.note: when the edges go away, the outer portions at each end of the word are cut off

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A liberal European politician slowly sidles towards the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: The edges removed are three letters at each end of progressive, leaving its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out of a place, the noun sense of exit.

clue.text: One and only bit of fun I queried

indicators.note: a bit of something is a piece of it, so the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone questions a one-off bit of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique is the sole example of its kind, which is what one and only means.

clue.text: Persuade uncle fine is out of order

indicators.note: letters that are out of order are jumbled and must be rearranged into the right sequence

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to talk an uncle into paying a fine that is improper.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence someone is to sway or persuade them, a close verb synonym.

clue.text: Bury in back half of cemetery without your head

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'without' means lacking, so the letter named next is dropped from what comes before it

parts.note: the last four of the eight letters of cemetery

indicators.note: 'head' keeps only the first letter of 'your'

parts.note: the first letter of your

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to bury a beheaded body at the back of the graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of cemetery loses the first letter of 'your' before joining IN to make INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, which is exactly what bury means.

clue.text: Time off to slow down, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is chosen for how it is pronounced, not how it is written

parts.note: to brake is to slow a vehicle down, and it is pronounced like its twin spelling

explanation.surface: Someone says that taking a holiday is how to slow the pace of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a rest period or short holiday, time away from work.

clue.text: Surprisingly quiet about boxer having special attributes

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next item
something that turns out surprisingly is not in the expected form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged
Muhammad Ali, the most famous boxer, is a crossword regular
S is a standard abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A boxer is unexpectedly calm and gifted in rare ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split around the famous boxer rather than sitting whole beside him, and the special letter is tacked on last.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualities are characteristics or traits, which is the noun sense of attributes.

clue.text: Increase luck without beginning to follow directions

indicators.note: lacking its beginning means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: east and north, two compass points
chance and luck are synonyms

explanation.surface: Advice to improve your fortune by doing as you are told rather than starting from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' places the shortened luck word after the compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to improve or heighten it, so it works as the verb increase.

clue.text: Cruel to let shares crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things into pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It is unkind to allow the stock market to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartless lacks compassion, so the word is a synonym of cruel.

clue.text: Hint at member to go quietly

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint
a member is a limb or part of the body, here a toe

explanation.surface: Someone signals to a club member that it is time to leave discreetly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk on the balls of your feet so as to move silently.

clue.text: Knew more complaining reportedly causes serious illness

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: knew sounds like new, and more complaining is moanier

explanation.surface: Someone better informed is also more inclined to grumble, and gets very ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The P at the start is silent, so the illness is said like the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is an infection inflaming the lungs, which can be a life-threatening illness.

clue.text: He appears in court for the French state against the Queen

parts.note: la is a French word for the
WY is the postal abbreviation for Wyoming, a US state
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A court case is described: a prosecutor appears for France in a suit against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' here just means next to, putting the state beside the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer is the professional who represents clients and so is a person who appears in court.

clue.text: Was King George in control before Edward?

definitions.text: Was King George in control before Edward?

parts.note: to reign is to be in control as a monarch
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A history quiz question about whether George ruled Britain before Edward did.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a question about George V ruling before Edward VIII, and also the recipe: the word for ruling, then a short form of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A king who held the throne reigned; the past tense matches the clue's 'was'.

clue.text: Gasp for a brew of herb tea

indicators.note: a brew is made by mixing things together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate for a cup of herbal tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to breathe in sharply, so breathe covers the same action of drawing air.

clue.text: Better than very regularly wearing tie

indicators.note: the thing being worn is around its wearer, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bond is a tie that binds

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone looks better than ever when wearing a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like the garment, but it means a link or bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond can mean exceeding or surpassing, so it stands for better than, as in 'beyond expectations'.

clue.text: Starts to engage underground cell to put messages into code

indicators.note: the starts of a word are its opening letters, here the first two

parts.note: the opening two letters of engage
a crypt is an underground vault or chamber

explanation.surface: Spies are told to start work in a basement cell to scramble their messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To encrypt is to convert information into a cipher, so it means putting messages into code.

clue.text: England loses heart after move to the rear is supported

indicators.note: losing the heart means the whole middle of the word goes, leaving only its ends

parts.note: to go back is to move to the rear
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: The England team lose confidence after a defensive retreat, yet are backed by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the trimmed country after the rear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be backed is to be supported or endorsed, as with a candidate or a bet.

clue.text: Writer with personal magnetism has unknown power

parts.note: an author is a writer
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A charismatic novelist wields mysterious influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Authority is the right or ability to command, a synonym of power in that sense.

clue.text: Eyes up internet company lacking drive with customers finally

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the next word's letters are removed

parts.note: Google is the internet search giant
go means energy or drive

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of customers

explanation.surface: A tech firm without ambition looks at its clients.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone lecherously, which is what eyeing them up means.

clue.text: Charming mother caught going after soldier

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a GI is an American soldier
C stands for caught in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A delightful mother is arrested while chasing a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, magic means enchanting or wonderful, so it can stand for charming.

clue.text: Interrogate gutless grenadier wrongfully

indicators.note: without its guts a word has lost its insides, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of grenadier
ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A cowardly soldier is unjustly questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to question them intensively, as police do to a suspect.

clue.text: Pay obeisance to king born to take on the Spanish

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
né, the masculine of née, marks a man's name at birth
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A born king must bow down before taking on Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to go down on bended knee, the classic gesture of deference or homage.

clue.text: Nobody not ninety is dancing

indicators.note: dancers move about, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: No one under ninety is out on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an unimportant person, and a nonentity is exactly such an insignificant figure.

clue.text: Out of service, police officers took drugs

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: Officers found using drugs have been suspended from duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused is no longer employed or operating, which is what out of service means.

clue.text: Amateur allowed in play

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in ham radio or a ham actor
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An unpaid actor gets a part in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's tragedy, so it is an example of a play.
